name: SlowMag
why: His preferred chloride form; his total elemental magnesium is much higher (~1 g from several forms).

name: Low-dose aspirin
why: Lifespan 83 mg; Attia lukewarm. Not USPSTF advice for starting after age 60.

name: Glutathione (Entity LumeniX)
description: Reduced glutathione delivered as a WaferiX sublingual wafer (Entity Health). Dissolves under the tongue; company claims nanoparticle delivery that bypasses the gut. Marketed mainly for skin (gloss, elasticity, fine lines) plus antioxidant/liver support.
primaryProponent: Entity Health (product trial), not Attia/Patrick/Sinclair. Rhonda Patrick is the nearest of Douglas's three sources, but she raises glutathione with sulforaphane rather than oral GSH.
why: Company-sponsored skin trial used 200 mg/day for 4 weeks then 100 mg maintenance — his 100 mg is the maintenance dose. Oral glutathione capsules are poorly absorbed; the wafer is the claimed workaround.
notes: Not a staple of Attia, Patrick, or Sinclair. Closest related longevity approaches are sulforaphane (Patrick) and GlyNAC (glycine + NAC).

name: Neuro-Mag
description: Magnesium L-threonate (Magtein), the form studied for raising cerebrospinal magnesium. Douglas also takes SlowMag (chloride) by day; this is a second magnesium form at night.
why: Night magnesium in the Magtein form Attia takes; marketed for memory/brain Mg. Complements daytime SlowMag.
notes: Drive #276: L-threonate at night as part of ~1 g elemental magnesium. Magtein/Liu for the form. Patrick uses glycinate instead.

name: Glycine
description: Amino acid used at bedtime for sleep; also a collagen building block. 1 g is below the ~3 g dose in Inagawa/Bannai sleep studies. Not the high-dose GlyNAC protocol.
why: Sleep support at a modest 1 g nightly.
notes: Closest of Douglas's preferred sources; bedtime glycine appears in later stack notes. Patrick's night item is myo-inositol.

name: Creatine
description: Creatine monohydrate; strength adjunct with resistance training; possible cognitive support under stress and aging.
why: Drive #369 and Patrick discuss ~5 g/day; Diamandis also lists ~5 g/day. Human RCTs and meta-analyses in older adults show modest strength gains when combined with resistance training.

name: Spermidine
primaryProponent: Frank Madeo; Sinclair has discussed it

name: Tirzepatide (GLP-1 / GIP agonist) — microdose
description: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist (Mounjaro/Zepbound class). Diamandis lists a Sunday-only microdose in his April 2026 MetaTrends protocol (Abundance Summit notes with Sinclair). Beyond weight loss he cites heart/brain signals; SELECT/FLOW outcome evidence is at full therapeutic doses, not microdose.
why: Considering for longevity/metabolic effects at a microdose, not full obesity titration. Exact mg not stated in Diamandis's public 2026 writeup — leave dose as microdose/unpublished until Douglas supplies a number.
notes: Apr 21 2026 MetaTrends: 'Tirzepatide (microdose): Sunday only'. Sinclair discussed the space with him; Attia discusses GLP-1s clinically but is not the source of this microdose schedule. Rx. Muscle-loss risk if appetite drops without protein + resistance training. Not medical advice.
